hinglish_roman: Itihaas mein quadratic equations hal karne mein kiska yogdaan raha?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A prayer hall must have a carpet area of 300 m², with length one metre more than twice its breadth. Form the equation and find the dimensions.
hinglish_roman: Ek prayer hall ka carpet area 300 m² hona chahiye, aur lambai chaudai ke do gune se ek metre zyada. Equation banao aur maap nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Check whether these are quadratic equations: (i) (x − 2)² + 1 = 2x − 3 (ii) x(x + 1) + 8 = (x + 2)(x − 2) (iii) x(2x + 3) = x² + 1 (iv) (x + 2)³ = x³ − 4. What is the lesson?
hinglish_roman: Jaancho ki ye quadratic equations hain ya nahi: (i) (x − 2)² + 1 = 2x − 3 (ii) x(x + 1) + 8 = (x + 2)(x − 2) (iii) x(2x + 3) = x² + 1 (iv) (x + 2)³ = x³ − 4. Isse kya seekh milti hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Which of these are quadratic? (i) (x + 1)² = 2(x − 3) (ii) x² − 2x = (−2)(3 − x) (iii) (x − 2)(x + 1) = (x − 1)(x + 3) (iv) (x − 3)(2x + 1) = x(x + 5) (v) (2x − 1)(x − 3) = (x + 5)(x − 1) (vi) x² + 3x + 1 = (x − 2)² (vii) (x + 2)³ = 2x(x² − 1) (viii) x³ − 4x² − x + 1 = (x − 2)³
hinglish_roman: Inmein se kaun quadratic hain? (i) (x + 1)² = 2(x − 3) (ii) x² − 2x = (−2)(3 − x) (iii) (x − 2)(x + 1) = (x − 1)(x + 3) (iv) (x − 3)(2x + 1) = x(x + 5) (v) (2x − 1)(x − 3) = (x + 5)(x − 1) (vi) x² + 3x + 1 = (x − 2)² (vii) (x + 2)³ = 2x(x² − 1) (viii) x³ − 4x² − x + 1 = (x − 2)³

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Represent as quadratic equations: (i) a rectangular plot of area 528 m² with length one more than twice its breadth; (ii) two consecutive positive integers with product 306; (iii) Rohan's mother is 26 years older and the product of their ages 3 years from now is 360; (iv) a train covers 480 km, and 8 km/h less speed would take 3 hours more.
hinglish_roman: Quadratic equations ke roop mein likho: (i) 528 m² ka rectangular plot jiski lambai chaudai ke do gune se ek zyada hai; (ii) do lagaataar positive integers jinka guna 306 hai; (iii) Rohan ki maa usse 26 saal badi hai aur 3 saal baad unki umar ka guna 360 hoga; (iv) train 480 km chalti hai, aur 8 km/h kam speed pe 3 ghante zyada lagte.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is a root of a quadratic equation? How many roots can it have?
hinglish_roman: Quadratic equation ka root kya hota hai? Uske kitne roots ho sakte hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the roots by factorisation: (a) 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 (b) 6x² − x − 2 = 0 (c) 3x² − 2√6x + 2 = 0.
hinglish_roman: Factorisation se roots nikaalo: (a) 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 (b) 6x² − x − 2 = 0 (c) 3x² − 2√6x + 2 = 0.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Solve by factorisation: (i) x² − 3x − 10 = 0 (ii) 2x² + x − 6 = 0 (iii) √2x² + 7x + 5√2 = 0 (iv) 2x² − x + 1/8 = 0 (v) 100x² − 20x + 1 = 0
hinglish_roman: Factorisation se hal karo: (i) x² − 3x − 10 = 0 (ii) 2x² + x − 6 = 0 (iii) √2x² + 7x + 5√2 = 0 (iv) 2x² − x + 1/8 = 0 (v) 100x² − 20x + 1 = 0

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) John and Jivanti together have 45 marbles; after each loses 5, the product of what they have is 124. How many did each have? (b) A cottage industry's cost per toy is 55 minus the number of toys made; one day the total cost was ₹750. How many toys were made?
hinglish_roman: (a) John aur Jivanti ke paas milaakar 45 kanche hain; dono 5-5 kho dete hain to bache hue kanchon ka guna 124 hai. Har ek ke paas kitne the? (b) Ek cottage industry mein ek khilone ki laagat 55 minus banaye gaye khilone hai; ek din kul laagat ₹750 thi. Kitne khilone bane?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find two numbers whose sum is 27 and product 182. (b) Find two consecutive positive integers the sum of whose squares is 365.
hinglish_roman: (a) Do numbers nikaalo jinka jod 27 aur guna 182 hai. (b) Do lagaataar positive integers nikaalo jinke vargon ka jod 365 hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) The altitude of a right triangle is 7 cm less than its base and the hypotenuse is 13 cm. Find the other two sides. (b) The cost of each pottery article is ₹3 more than twice the number made, and the total cost is ₹90. Find the number of articles and cost of each.
hinglish_roman: (a) Ek right triangle ki oonchai uske base se 7 cm kam hai aur hypotenuse 13 cm hai. Baaki do bhujaayein nikaalo. (b) Har mitti ke saamaan ki laagat banaye gaye saamaan ke do gune se ₹3 zyada hai, aur kul laagat ₹90 hai. Saamaan ki sankhya aur har ek ki laagat nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: State the quadratic formula. What is the discriminant and how does it decide the nature of roots?
hinglish_roman: Quadratic formula batao. Discriminant kya hai aur ye roots ka nature kaise tay karta hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the discriminant and nature of roots: (a) 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0 (b) 3x² − 2x + 1/3 = 0. Find the roots if real.
hinglish_roman: Discriminant aur roots ka nature nikaalo: (a) 2x² − 4x + 3 = 0 (b) 3x² − 2x + 1/3 = 0. Real hon to roots bhi nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A pole is to be erected on the boundary of a circular park of diameter 13 m so that the difference of its distances from two diametrically opposite gates A and B is 7 m. Is it possible? If yes, where?
hinglish_roman: 13 m diameter waale gol park ki boundary pe ek khamba aise lagaana hai ki aamne-saamne ke do gates A aur B se uski doori ka fark 7 m ho. Kya ye sambhav hai? Agar haan, toh kahaan?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the nature of roots and the roots if real: (i) 2x² − 3x + 5 = 0 (ii) 3x² − 4√3x + 4 = 0 (iii) 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0.
hinglish_roman: Roots ka nature batao aur real hon to roots nikaalo: (i) 2x² − 3x + 5 = 0 (ii) 3x² − 4√3x + 4 = 0 (iii) 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find k so that each equation has two equal roots: (i) 2x² + kx + 3 = 0 (ii) kx(x − 2) + 6 = 0.
hinglish_roman: k ki value nikaalo taaki har equation ke do barabar roots hon: (i) 2x² + kx + 3 = 0 (ii) kx(x − 2) + 6 = 0.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Check feasibility: (a) a rectangular mango grove with length twice its breadth and area 800 m²; (b) two friends whose ages sum to 20 and whose ages four years ago had product 48; (c) a rectangular park of perimeter 80 m and area 400 m².
hinglish_roman: Sambhav hai ya nahi jaancho: (a) aam ka baag jiski lambai chaudai ki do guni aur area 800 m² ho; (b) do dost jinki umar ka jod 20 hai aur chaar saal pehle umar ka guna 48 tha; (c) rectangular park jiska perimeter 80 m aur area 400 m² ho.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: The equation x² + 7 = 0 has: (a) two distinct real roots (b) two equal real roots (c) no real roots (d) one real root
hinglish_roman: Equation x² + 7 = 0 ke: (a) do alag real roots (b) do barabar real roots (c) koi real root nahi (d) ek real root

subject: Mathematics
original_english: True or False: Every quadratic equation has exactly two real roots.
hinglish_roman: Sahi ya Galat: Har quadratic equation ke theek do real roots hote hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is an arithmetic progression (AP)? What is its common difference and general form?
hinglish_roman: Arithmetic progression (AP) kya hoti hai? Iska common difference aur general form kya hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Give real-life examples of patterns from the chapter, and say which of them are APs.
hinglish_roman: Chapter se real-life patterns ke udaharan do, aur batao inmein se kaun AP hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Differentiate between a finite AP and an infinite AP. What minimum information is needed to know an AP?
hinglish_roman: Finite AP aur infinite AP mein antar batao. AP jaanne ke liye kam se kam kya jaankari chahiye?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Which of these form an AP? If so, write the next two terms: (i) 4, 10, 16, 22, … (ii) 1, −1, −3, −5, … (iii) −2, 2, −2, 2, … (iv) 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, …
hinglish_roman: Inmein se kaun AP hain? Agar hain toh agle do terms likho: (i) 4, 10, 16, 22, … (ii) 1, −1, −3, −5, … (iii) −2, 2, −2, 2, … (iv) 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, …

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Which situations give an AP and why? (i) Taxi fare: ₹15 for the first km, ₹8 for each additional km. (ii) Air in a cylinder when a pump removes 1/4 of the remaining air each time. (iii) Cost of digging a well: ₹150 for the first metre, rising by ₹50 per subsequent metre. (iv) ₹10000 at 8% compound interest per annum.
hinglish_roman: Kaun si sthitiyon mein AP banti hai aur kyun? (i) Taxi kiraaya: pehle km ka ₹15, har agle km ka ₹8. (ii) Cylinder mein hawa jab pump har baar bachi hawa ka 1/4 nikaalta hai. (iii) Kuaan khodne ki laagat: pehle metre ki ₹150, har agle metre pe ₹50 badhti hai. (iv) ₹10000 pe 8% saalana compound interest.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Derive the formula for the nth term of an AP using Reena's salary example.
hinglish_roman: Reena ki salary ke udaharan se AP ke nth term ka formula nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the 10th term of 2, 7, 12, … (b) Which term of 21, 18, 15, … is −81? Is any term 0? (c) Is 301 a term of 5, 11, 17, 23, …?
hinglish_roman: (a) 2, 7, 12, … ka 10va term nikaalo. (b) 21, 18, 15, … ka kaunsa term −81 hai? Kya koi term 0 hai? (c) Kya 301, 5, 11, 17, 23, … ka term hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 3? (b) How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 7? (c) How many multiples of 4 lie between 10 and 250?
hinglish_roman: (a) Kitne do-ank numbers 3 se divisible hain? (b) Kitne teen-ank numbers 7 se divisible hain? (c) 10 aur 250 ke beech 4 ke kitne multiples hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the 11th term from the last of 10, 7, 4, …, −62. (b) Find the 20th term from the last of 3, 8, 13, …, 253.
hinglish_roman: (a) 10, 7, 4, …, −62 ka aakhri se 11va term nikaalo. (b) 3, 8, 13, …, 253 ka aakhri se 20va term nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the AP whose 3rd term is 5 and 7th term is 9. (b) Find the 31st term of an AP whose 11th term is 38 and 16th term is 73. (c) The 3rd and 9th terms are 4 and −8; which term is zero?
hinglish_roman: (a) Woh AP nikaalo jiska 3ra term 5 aur 7va term 9 hai. (b) Jis AP ka 11va term 38 aur 16va term 73 hai, uska 31va term nikaalo. (c) 3ra aur 9va term 4 aur −8 hain; kaunsa term zero hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) ₹1000 is invested at 8% simple interest. Do the yearly interests form an AP? Find the interest at the end of 30 years. (b) A flower bed has 23 rose plants in the first row, 21 in the second, 19 in the third, …, and 5 in the last. How many rows are there?
hinglish_roman: (a) ₹1000, 8% simple interest pe lagaaye gaye. Kya saalana interest AP banate hain? 30 saal ke ant mein interest nikaalo. (b) Phoolon ki kyaari mein pehli line mein 23 gulab, doosri mein 21, teesri mein 19, …, aur aakhri mein 5 hain. Kitni lines hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Subba Rao started in 1995 at ₹5000 a year with ₹200 increments. In which year did his income reach ₹7000? (b) Ramkali saved ₹5 in the first week and increased weekly savings by ₹1.75. In which week do her savings become ₹20.75? (c) For what n are the nth terms of 63, 65, 67, … and 3, 10, 17, … equal?
hinglish_roman: (a) Subba Rao ne 1995 mein ₹5000 saalana se shuru kiya aur har saal ₹200 badhotri mili. Kis saal unki income ₹7000 pahunchi? (b) Ramkali ne pehle hafte ₹5 bachaaye aur har hafte ₹1.75 badhaaye. Kis hafte bachat ₹20.75 hogi? (c) Kis n ke liye 63, 65, 67, … aur 3, 10, 17, … ke nth terms barabar hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Which term of 3, 15, 27, 39, … is 132 more than its 54th term? (b) Two APs have the same common difference and their 100th terms differ by 100. What is the difference between their 1000th terms? (c) The 17th term exceeds the 10th by 7. Find d.
hinglish_roman: (a) 3, 15, 27, 39, … ka kaunsa term uske 54ve term se 132 zyada hai? (b) Do APs ka common difference same hai aur unke 100ve terms ka fark 100 hai. Unke 1000ve terms ka fark kya hai? (c) 17va term 10ve se 7 zyada hai. d nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How did Gauss add 1 to 100, and how does the same idea give the sum of the first n terms of an AP?
hinglish_roman: Gauss ne 1 se 100 tak kaise joda, aur wahi tareeka AP ke pehle n terms ka jod kaise deta hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Shakila puts ₹100, 150, 200, … in her daughter's money box on each birthday. How much is collected by the 21st birthday? (b) Find the sum of the first 22 terms of 8, 3, −2, …
hinglish_roman: (a) Shakila apni beti ke gullak mein har birthday pe ₹100, 150, 200, … daalti hai. 21ve birthday tak kitna jama hoga? (b) 8, 3, −2, … ke pehle 22 terms ka jod nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) S₁₄ = 1050 and a = 10; find the 20th term. (b) How many terms of 24, 21, 18, … give sum 78? Why are there two answers?
hinglish_roman: (a) S₁₄ = 1050 aur a = 10; 20va term nikaalo. (b) 24, 21, 18, … ke kitne terms ka jod 78 hai? Do jawab kyun aate hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the sum of the first 1000 positive integers and of the first n positive integers. (b) Find the sum of the first 24 terms when aₙ = 3 + 2n. (c) Find the sum of odd numbers between 0 and 50.
hinglish_roman: (a) Pehle 1000 positive integers aur pehle n positive integers ka jod nikaalo. (b) aₙ = 3 + 2n ho toh pehle 24 terms ka jod nikaalo. (c) 0 aur 50 ke beech odd numbers ka jod nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A TV manufacturer made 600 sets in the 3rd year and 700 in the 7th year, increasing uniformly. Find (i) the 1st-year production (ii) the 10th-year production (iii) the total in the first 7 years.
hinglish_roman: TV banane waale ne 3re saal 600 aur 7ve saal 700 sets banaaye, ek samaan badhotri se. Nikaalo (i) pehle saal ka production (ii) 10ve saal ka production (iii) pehle 7 saal ka kul production.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: In an AP: (i) a = 5, d = 3, aₙ = 50: find n and Sₙ. (ii) a = 7, a₁₃ = 35: find d and S₁₃. (iii) a₃ = 15, S₁₀ = 125: find d and a₁₀. (iv) a = 2, d = 8, Sₙ = 90: find n and aₙ. (v) aₙ = 4, d = 2, Sₙ = −14: find n and a.
hinglish_roman: Ek AP mein: (i) a = 5, d = 3, aₙ = 50: n aur Sₙ nikaalo. (ii) a = 7, a₁₃ = 35: d aur S₁₃. (iii) a₃ = 15, S₁₀ = 125: d aur a₁₀. (iv) a = 2, d = 8, Sₙ = 90: n aur aₙ. (v) aₙ = 4, d = 2, Sₙ = −14: n aur a.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) How many terms of 9, 17, 25, … give 636? (b) S₇ = 49 and S₁₇ = 289; find Sₙ. (c) If Sₙ = 4n − n², find a₁, a₂, a₃, a₁₀ and aₙ.
hinglish_roman: (a) 9, 17, 25, … ke kitne terms ka jod 636 hai? (b) S₇ = 49 aur S₁₇ = 289; Sₙ nikaalo. (c) Agar Sₙ = 4n − n² ho, toh a₁, a₂, a₃, a₁₀ aur aₙ nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A contractor's delay penalty is ₹200, 250, 300, … per day. What is the total for 30 days? (b) ₹700 is split into seven prizes, each ₹20 less than the previous. Find the prizes. (c) Each of 3 sections of Classes I–XII plants trees equal to its class number. How many trees in all?
hinglish_roman: (a) Contractor ka der ka jurmaana roz ₹200, 250, 300, … hai. 30 din ka kul kitna? (b) ₹700 ko saat inaamon mein baanta, har inaam pichhle se ₹20 kam. Inaam nikaalo. (c) Class I–XII ke har class ke 3 sections apni class number jitne ped lagaate hain. Kul kitne ped?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) 200 logs are stacked with 20 in the bottom row, 19 in the next, and so on. How many rows, and how many logs in the top row? (b) In a potato race the bucket is 5 m from the first potato, and ten potatoes are placed 3 m apart. Each potato is fetched separately. What is the total distance run?
hinglish_roman: (a) 200 lakdiyaan aise rakhi hain: neeche ki line mein 20, agli mein 19, aur aise hi. Kitni lines hain aur sabse upar kitni lakdiyaan? (b) Potato race mein bucket pehle aaloo se 5 m door hai aur das aaloo 3 m ke fark pe hain. Har aaloo alag se laana hai. Kul kitna daudna padega?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Which term of 121, 117, 113, … is its first negative term? (b) The 3rd and 7th terms sum to 6 and have product 8. Find the sum of the first 16 terms. (c) Houses are numbered 1 to 49. Find x such that the sum of numbers before house x equals the sum after it.
hinglish_roman: (a) 121, 117, 113, … ka pehla negative term kaunsa hai? (b) 3re aur 7ve term ka jod 6 aur guna 8 hai. Pehle 16 terms ka jod nikaalo. (c) Ghar 1 se 49 tak numbered hain. x nikaalo jiske pehle ke gharon ke numbers ka jod uske baad waalon ke jod ke barabar ho.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: If a, b, c are in AP, then b = ______ and b is called the ______ of a and c.
hinglish_roman: Agar a, b, c AP mein hain, toh b = ______ aur b ko a aur c ka ______ kehte hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What are similar figures? How are they different from congruent figures?
hinglish_roman: Similar figures kya hote hain? Ye congruent figures se kaise alag hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: When are two polygons similar? Why is one condition alone not enough?
hinglish_roman: Do polygons kab similar hote hain? Sirf ek shart kaafi kyun nahi hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How does a photographer's enlargement of photos illustrate similarity? Are two same-size photos of a person at age 10 and 40 similar?
hinglish_roman: Photographer ka photo bada karna similarity ko kaise samjhaata hai? Kya ek insaan ki 10 aur 40 saal ki umar ki same size ki photos similar hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Fill in the blanks: (i) All circles are ______. (ii) All squares are ______. (iii) All ______ triangles are similar. (iv) Two polygons with the same number of sides are similar if their corresponding angles are ______ and their corresponding sides are ______.
hinglish_roman: Khaali jagah bharo: (i) Saare circles ______ hain. (ii) Saare squares ______ hain. (iii) Saare ______ triangles similar hain. (iv) Same number of sides waale do polygons similar hain agar unke corresponding angles ______ hon aur corresponding sides ______ hon.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem).
hinglish_roman: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem) batao aur prove karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: State the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem. How is it shown?
hinglish_roman: Basic Proportionality Theorem ka converse batao. Ise kaise dikhaate hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) If DE ∥ BC in △ABC, prove AD/AB = AE/AC. (b) ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, and EF ∥ AB with E on AD and F on BC. Show AE/ED = BF/FC.
hinglish_roman: (a) △ABC mein DE ∥ BC ho toh prove karo AD/AB = AE/AC. (b) ABCD trapezium hai jisme AB ∥ DC, aur EF ∥ AB jahan E AD pe aur F BC pe hai. Dikhao AE/ED = BF/FC.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: E and F are on sides PQ and PR of △PQR. Is EF ∥ QR? (i) PE = 3.9, EQ = 3, PF = 3.6, FR = 2.4 cm (ii) PE = 4, QE = 4.5, PF = 8, RF = 9 cm (iii) PQ = 1.28, PR = 2.56, PE = 0.18, PF = 0.36 cm
hinglish_roman: △PQR ki sides PQ aur PR pe E aur F hain. Kya EF ∥ QR hai? (i) PE = 3.9, EQ = 3, PF = 3.6, FR = 2.4 cm (ii) PE = 4, QE = 4.5, PF = 8, RF = 9 cm (iii) PQ = 1.28, PR = 2.56, PE = 0.18, PF = 0.36 cm

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Using Theorem 6.1, prove that a line through the mid-point of one side of a triangle parallel to another side bisects the third side. (b) ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC whose diagonals meet at O. Show AO/BO = CO/DO.
hinglish_roman: (a) Theorem 6.1 se prove karo ki triangle ki ek side ke mid-point se doosri side ke parallel kheenchi line teesri side ko bisect karti hai. (b) ABCD trapezium hai, AB ∥ DC, aur diagonals O pe milte hain. Dikhao AO/BO = CO/DO.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: List the criteria for similarity of two triangles.
hinglish_roman: Do triangles ki similarity ke criteria batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: For polygons both conditions (equal angles and proportional sides) are needed for similarity. Why is one enough for triangles? How should △ABC ~ △DEF be written?
hinglish_roman: Polygons ki similarity ke liye dono shartein (barabar angles aur proportional sides) chahiye. Triangles ke liye ek kaafi kyun hai? △ABC ~ △DEF kaise likhte hain?

subject: Mathematics
hinglish_roman: △ABC mein AB = 3.8, BC = 6, CA = 3√3, ∠A = 80°, ∠B = 60°. △PQR mein RQ = 7.6, QP = 12, PR = 6√3. ∠P nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) If PQ ∥ RS and PS, QR meet at O, prove △POQ ~ △SOR. (b) If OA·OB = OC·OD (AC and BD meeting at O), show ∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D.
hinglish_roman: (a) Agar PQ ∥ RS aur PS, QR, O pe milte hain, toh prove karo △POQ ~ △SOR. (b) Agar OA·OB = OC·OD (AC aur BD, O pe milte hain), toh dikhao ∠A = ∠C aur ∠B = ∠D.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A girl 90 cm tall walks away from a lamp-post at 1.2 m/s. The lamp is 3.6 m above the ground. Find the length of her shadow after 4 seconds.
hinglish_roman: 90 cm lambi ladki lamp-post se 1.2 m/s ki speed se door chal rahi hai. Lamp zameen se 3.6 m upar hai. 4 second baad uski parchhaai ki lambai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A vertical pole 6 m long casts a 4 m shadow while a tower casts a 28 m shadow at the same time. Find the tower's height. (b) If △ODC ~ △OBA, ∠BOC = 125° and ∠CDO = 70°, find ∠DOC, ∠DCO and ∠OAB.
hinglish_roman: (a) 6 m lamba khamba 4 m ki parchhaai banata hai jabki usi samay tower 28 m ki parchhaai banata hai. Tower ki oonchai nikaalo. (b) Agar △ODC ~ △OBA, ∠BOC = 125° aur ∠CDO = 70°, toh ∠DOC, ∠DCO aur ∠OAB nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: D is a point on side BC of △ABC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. Show that CA² = CB·CD.
hinglish_roman: △ABC ki side BC pe point D aisa hai ki ∠ADC = ∠BAC. Dikhao ki CA² = CB·CD.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: CM and RN are medians of △ABC and △PQR, and △ABC ~ △PQR. Prove (i) △AMC ~ △PNR (ii) CM/RN = AB/PQ.
hinglish_roman: CM aur RN, △ABC aur △PQR ki medians hain, aur △ABC ~ △PQR. Prove karo (i) △AMC ~ △PNR (ii) CM/RN = AB/PQ.

subject: Mathematics
original_english:
Assertion (A): Two triangles with sides 3, 6, 8 cm and 4.5, 9, 12 cm have equal corresponding angles.
Reason (R): If the sides of one triangle are proportional to the sides of another, their corresponding angles are equal.
hinglish_roman:
Assertion (A): 3, 6, 8 cm aur 4.5, 9, 12 cm sides waale do triangles ke corresponding angles barabar hain.
Reason (R): Agar ek triangle ki sides doosre ki sides ke proportional hon, toh unke corresponding angles barabar hote hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: True or False: (i) All congruent figures are similar. (ii) All similar figures are congruent. (iii) Two isosceles triangles are always similar.
hinglish_roman: Sahi ya Galat: (i) Saare congruent figures similar hote hain. (ii) Saare similar figures congruent hote hain. (iii) Do isosceles triangles hamesha similar hote hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Which Greek mathematician stated that the ratio of any two corresponding sides in two equiangular triangles is always the same?
hinglish_roman: Kis Greek mathematician ne kaha ki do equiangular triangles mein kinhi do corresponding sides ka ratio hamesha same hota hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What are the abscissa and ordinate of a point? What do points on the axes look like?
hinglish_roman: Kisi point ka abscissa aur ordinate kya hota hai? Axes pe points kaise dikhte hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Why is coordinate geometry useful, and where is it applied?
hinglish_roman: Coordinate geometry kyun upyogi hai, aur kahaan use hoti hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Derive the distance formula between P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂).
hinglish_roman: P(x₁, y₁) aur Q(x₂, y₂) ke beech ka distance formula nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the distance between: (i) (2, 3) and (4, 1) (ii) (−5, 7) and (−1, 3) (iii) (a, b) and (−a, −b) (iv) (0, 0) and (36, 15). Use (iv) to find the distance between town A and town B, which is 36 km east and 15 km north of A.
hinglish_roman: Doori nikaalo: (i) (2, 3) aur (4, 1) (ii) (−5, 7) aur (−1, 3) (iii) (a, b) aur (−a, −b) (iv) (0, 0) aur (36, 15). (iv) se town A aur town B ki doori nikaalo, jahan B, A se 36 km poorab aur 15 km uttar mein hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Do the points (3, 2), (−2, −3) and (2, 3) form a triangle? If so, what type?
hinglish_roman: Kya points (3, 2), (−2, −3) aur (2, 3) triangle banaate hain? Agar haan, toh kaisa?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Show that (1, 7), (4, 2), (−1, −1) and (−4, 4) are the vertices of a square.
hinglish_roman: Dikhao ki (1, 7), (4, 2), (−1, −1) aur (−4, 4) ek square ke vertices hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Ashima, Bharti and Camella sit at A(3, 1), B(6, 4) and C(8, 6). Are they in a line? (b) Are (1, 5), (2, 3) and (−2, −11) collinear?
hinglish_roman: (a) Ashima, Bharti aur Camella A(3, 1), B(6, 4) aur C(8, 6) pe baithi hain. Kya ve ek line mein hain? (b) Kya (1, 5), (2, 3) aur (−2, −11) collinear hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Name the quadrilateral formed, if any: (i) (−1, −2), (1, 0), (−1, 2), (−3, 0) (ii) (−3, 5), (3, 1), (0, 3), (−1, −4) (iii) (4, 5), (7, 6), (4, 3), (1, 2). Also check whether (5, −2), (6, 4), (7, −2) form an isosceles triangle.
hinglish_roman: Kaun sa quadrilateral banta hai, agar banta hai: (i) (−1, −2), (1, 0), (−1, 2), (−3, 0) (ii) (−3, 5), (3, 1), (0, 3), (−1, −4) (iii) (4, 5), (7, 6), (4, 3), (1, 2). Saath hi jaancho ki (5, −2), (6, 4), (7, −2) isosceles triangle banaate hain ya nahi.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find a relation between x and y if (x, y) is equidistant from (7, 1) and (3, 5). (b) Find the point on the y-axis equidistant from A(6, 5) and B(−4, 3).
hinglish_roman: (a) Agar (x, y), (7, 1) aur (3, 5) se barabar doori pe hai toh x aur y ka sambandh nikaalo. (b) y-axis pe woh point nikaalo jo A(6, 5) aur B(−4, 3) se barabar doori pe ho.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the point on the x-axis equidistant from (2, −5) and (−2, 9). (b) Find y if P(2, −3) and Q(10, y) are 10 units apart. (c) Q(0, 1) is equidistant from P(5, −3) and R(x, 6); find x, QR and PR. (d) Find the relation if (x, y) is equidistant from (3, 6) and (−3, 4).
hinglish_roman: (a) x-axis pe (2, −5) aur (−2, 9) se barabar doori waala point nikaalo. (b) P(2, −3) aur Q(10, y) 10 units door hain toh y nikaalo. (c) Q(0, 1), P(5, −3) aur R(x, 6) se barabar door hai; x, QR aur PR nikaalo. (d) (x, y), (3, 6) aur (−3, 4) se barabar door ho toh sambandh nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: State the section formula and the mid-point formula. Derive the section formula briefly.
hinglish_roman: Section formula aur mid-point formula batao. Section formula sankshep mein nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A telephone company wants a relay tower P on the line between towns A and B, with its distance from B twice its distance from A. With A at the origin and B at (36, 15), where should P be?
hinglish_roman: Telephone company towns A aur B ke beech line pe relay tower P lagaana chahti hai, jiski B se doori A se doori ki dugni ho. A origin pe aur B (36, 15) pe ho toh P kahaan hona chahiye?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the point dividing the join of (4, −3) and (8, 5) in the ratio 3 : 1 internally. (b) Find the point dividing the join of (−1, 7) and (4, −3) in the ratio 2 : 3.
hinglish_roman: (a) (4, −3) aur (8, 5) ko jodne waale segment ko andar se 3 : 1 mein baantne waala point nikaalo. (b) (−1, 7) aur (4, −3) ke join ko 2 : 3 mein baantne waala point nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In what ratio does (−4, 6) divide the join of A(−6, 10) and B(3, −8)? (b) In what ratio does (−1, 6) divide the join of (−3, 10) and (6, −8)?
hinglish_roman: (a) (−4, 6), A(−6, 10) aur B(3, −8) ke join ko kis ratio mein baantta hai? (b) (−1, 6), (−3, 10) aur (6, −8) ke join ko kis ratio mein baantta hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the points of trisection of the join of A(2, −2) and B(−7, 4). (b) Find the points of trisection of the join of (4, −1) and (−2, −3). (c) Find the points dividing the join of A(−2, 2) and B(2, 8) into four equal parts.
hinglish_roman: (a) A(2, −2) aur B(−7, 4) ke join ke trisection points nikaalo. (b) (4, −1) aur (−2, −3) ke join ke trisection points nikaalo. (c) A(−2, 2) aur B(2, 8) ke join ko chaar barabar hisson mein baantne waale points nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In what ratio does the y-axis divide the join of (5, −6) and (−1, −4)? Find the point. (b) In what ratio does the x-axis divide the join of A(1, −5) and B(−4, 5)? Find the point.
hinglish_roman: (a) y-axis, (5, −6) aur (−1, −4) ke join ko kis ratio mein baantta hai? Point nikaalo. (b) x-axis, A(1, −5) aur B(−4, 5) ke join ko kis ratio mein baantta hai? Point nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A(6, 1), B(8, 2), C(9, 4), D(p, 3) form a parallelogram in order; find p. (b) (1, 2), (4, y), (x, 6), (3, 5) form a parallelogram in order; find x and y. (c) AB is a diameter of a circle with centre (2, −3) and B(1, 4); find A.
hinglish_roman: (a) A(6, 1), B(8, 2), C(9, 4), D(p, 3) kram se parallelogram banaate hain; p nikaalo. (b) (1, 2), (4, y), (x, 6), (3, 5) kram se parallelogram hain; x aur y nikaalo. (c) AB ek circle ka diameter hai jiska centre (2, −3) aur B(1, 4) hai; A nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A(−2, −2) and B(2, −4); find P on AB with AP = (3/7)AB. (b) Find the area of the rhombus with vertices (3, 0), (4, 5), (−1, 4), (−2, −1) in order.
hinglish_roman: (a) A(−2, −2) aur B(2, −4); AB pe P nikaalo jahan AP = (3/7)AB. (b) Vertices (3, 0), (4, 5), (−1, 4), (−2, −1) (kram se) waale rhombus ka area nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: On a school ground, lines are drawn 1 m apart and 100 flower pots are placed 1 m apart along AD. Niharika runs 1/4 of AD on the 2nd line and posts a green flag; Preet runs 1/5 of AD on the 8th line and posts a red flag. Find the distance between the flags and where Rashmi should post a blue flag halfway between them.
hinglish_roman: School ground pe lines 1 m ke fark pe hain aur AD ke saath 100 gamle 1 m ke fark pe rakhe hain. Niharika doosri line pe AD ka 1/4 daudkar hari jhandi lagaati hai; Preet aathvi line pe AD ka 1/5 daudkar laal jhandi lagaata hai. Jhandiyon ki doori aur Rashmi ki neeli jhandi ki jagah (theek beech mein) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: The mid-point of the segment joining (−2, 8) and (4, −2) is: (a) (1, 3) (b) (3, 5) (c) (2, 6) (d) (1, 5)
hinglish_roman: (−2, 8) aur (4, −2) ko jodne waale segment ka mid-point hai: (a) (1, 3) (b) (3, 5) (c) (2, 6) (d) (1, 5)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is trigonometry? Where does the word come from?
hinglish_roman: Trigonometry kya hai? Ye shabd kahaan se aaya?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Define the six trigonometric ratios of angle A in a right triangle ABC, right-angled at B.
hinglish_roman: B pe right-angled triangle ABC mein angle A ke chhe trigonometric ratios define karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How did the words 'sine' and 'cosine' originate?
hinglish_roman: 'Sine' aur 'cosine' shabd kaise bane?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Do trigonometric ratios of an angle depend on the size of the triangle? Explain.
hinglish_roman: Kya kisi angle ke trigonometric ratios triangle ke size pe nirbhar karte hain? Samjhaao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: True or False? Justify. (i) tan A is always less than 1. (ii) sec A = 12/5 for some angle A. (iii) cos A is the abbreviation for the cosecant of A. (iv) cot A is the product of cot and A. (v) sin θ = 4/3 for some angle θ.
hinglish_roman: Sahi ya Galat? Kaaran do. (i) tan A hamesha 1 se kam hota hai. (ii) Kisi angle A ke liye sec A = 12/5. (iii) cos A, cosecant of A ka sankshipt roop hai. (iv) cot A, cot aur A ka guna hai. (v) Kisi angle θ ke liye sin θ = 4/3.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Given tan A = 4/3, find the other trigonometric ratios. (b) If sin A = 1/3, find cos A.
hinglish_roman: (a) tan A = 4/3 diya hai, baaki trigonometric ratios nikaalo. (b) Agar sin A = 1/3 ho, toh cos A nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 24 cm and BC = 7 cm; find sin A, cos A, sin C, cos C. (b) If sin A = 3/4, find cos A and tan A. (c) If 15 cot A = 8, find sin A and sec A.
hinglish_roman: (a) B pe right-angled △ABC mein AB = 24 cm aur BC = 7 cm; sin A, cos A, sin C, cos C nikaalo. (b) sin A = 3/4 ho toh cos A aur tan A nikaalo. (c) 15 cot A = 8 ho toh sin A aur sec A nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Given sec θ = 13/12, find all other trigonometric ratios. (b) If cot θ = 7/8, evaluate (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ)/[(1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ)].
hinglish_roman: (a) sec θ = 13/12 diya hai, baaki saare trigonometric ratios nikaalo. (b) cot θ = 7/8 ho toh (1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ)/[(1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ)] nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In △ACB right-angled at C, AB = 29, BC = 21 and ∠ABC = θ. Find cos²θ + sin²θ and cos²θ − sin²θ. (b) In △OPQ right-angled at P, OP = 7 cm and OQ − PQ = 1 cm. Find sin Q and cos Q.
hinglish_roman: (a) C pe right-angled △ACB mein AB = 29, BC = 21 aur ∠ABC = θ. cos²θ + sin²θ aur cos²θ − sin²θ nikaalo. (b) P pe right-angled △OPQ mein OP = 7 cm aur OQ − PQ = 1 cm. sin Q aur cos Q nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In △PQR right-angled at Q, PR + QR = 25 cm and PQ = 5 cm. Find sin P, cos P, tan P. (b) If 3 cot A = 4, check whether (1 − tan²A)/(1 + tan²A) = cos²A − sin²A.
hinglish_roman: (a) Q pe right-angled △PQR mein PR + QR = 25 cm aur PQ = 5 cm. sin P, cos P, tan P nikaalo. (b) 3 cot A = 4 ho toh jaancho ki (1 − tan²A)/(1 + tan²A) = cos²A − sin²A hai ya nahi.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: If ∠B and ∠Q are acute angles with sin B = sin Q, prove ∠B = ∠Q.
hinglish_roman: Agar ∠B aur ∠Q acute angles hain aur sin B = sin Q, toh prove karo ∠B = ∠Q.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the trigonometric ratios of 45°, 30° and 60° using suitable triangles.
hinglish_roman: Sahi triangles lekar 45°, 30° aur 60° ke trigonometric ratios nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How are the trigonometric ratios of 0° and 90° defined? Which ones are not defined?
hinglish_roman: 0° aur 90° ke trigonometric ratios kaise define hote hain? Kaun se define nahi hote?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Evaluate: (i) sin 60° cos 30° + sin 30° cos 60° (ii) 2tan²45° + cos²30° − sin²60° (iii) (5cos²60° + 4sec²30° − tan²45°)/(sin²30° + cos²30°)
hinglish_roman: Value nikaalo: (i) sin 60° cos 30° + sin 30° cos 60° (ii) 2tan²45° + cos²30° − sin²60° (iii) (5cos²60° + 4sec²30° − tan²45°)/(sin²30° + cos²30°)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Evaluate: (i) cos 45°/(sec 30° + cosec 30°) (ii) (sin 30° + tan 45° − cosec 60°)/(sec 30° + cos 60° + cot 45°)
hinglish_roman: Value nikaalo: (i) cos 45°/(sec 30° + cosec 30°) (ii) (sin 30° + tan 45° − cosec 60°)/(sec 30° + cos 60° + cot 45°)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Choose the correct option: (i) 2tan 30°/(1 + tan²30°) = (A) sin 60° (B) cos 60° (C) tan 60° (D) sin 30°. (ii) (1 − tan²45°)/(1 + tan²45°) = (A) tan 90° (B) 1 (C) sin 45° (D) 0. (iii) sin 2A = 2 sin A is true when A = (A) 0° (B) 30° (C) 45° (D) 60°. (iv) 2tan 30°/(1 − tan²30°) = (A) cos 60° (B) sin 60° (C) tan 60° (D) sin 30°.
hinglish_roman: Sahi option chuno: (i) 2tan 30°/(1 + tan²30°) = (A) sin 60° (B) cos 60° (C) tan 60° (D) sin 30°. (ii) (1 − tan²45°)/(1 + tan²45°) = (A) tan 90° (B) 1 (C) sin 45° (D) 0. (iii) sin 2A = 2 sin A kab sahi hai, A = (A) 0° (B) 30° (C) 45° (D) 60°. (iv) 2tan 30°/(1 − tan²30°) = (A) cos 60° (B) sin 60° (C) tan 60° (D) sin 30°.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 5 cm and ∠ACB = 30°. Find BC and AC. (b) In △PQR right-angled at Q, PQ = 3 cm and PR = 6 cm. Find ∠QPR and ∠PRQ.
hinglish_roman: (a) B pe right-angled △ABC mein AB = 5 cm aur ∠ACB = 30°. BC aur AC nikaalo. (b) Q pe right-angled △PQR mein PQ = 3 cm aur PR = 6 cm. ∠QPR aur ∠PRQ nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) If sin(A − B) = 1/2 and cos(A + B) = 1/2 with 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B. (b) If tan(A + B) = √3 and tan(A − B) = 1/√3, find A and B. (c) In △ABC right-angled at B, tan A = 1/√3; find sin A cos C + cos A sin C.
hinglish_roman: (a) Agar sin(A − B) = 1/2 aur cos(A + B) = 1/2, jahan 0° < A + B ≤ 90° aur A > B, toh A aur B nikaalo. (b) tan(A + B) = √3 aur tan(A − B) = 1/√3 ho toh A aur B nikaalo. (c) B pe right-angled △ABC mein tan A = 1/√3; sin A cos C + cos A sin C nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: True or False? Justify. (i) sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B. (ii) sin θ increases as θ increases. (iii) cos θ increases as θ increases. (iv) sin θ = cos θ for all θ. (v) cot A is not defined for A = 0°.
hinglish_roman: Sahi ya Galat? Kaaran do. (i) sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B. (ii) θ badhne pe sin θ badhta hai. (iii) θ badhne pe cos θ badhta hai. (iv) Har θ ke liye sin θ = cos θ. (v) A = 0° ke liye cot A define nahi hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is a trigonometric identity? Derive the three fundamental identities and state where each holds.
hinglish_roman: Trigonometric identity kya hai? Teen mool identities nikaalo aur batao har ek kahaan sahi hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Given tan A = 1/√3, find the other ratios using identities. (b) Express cos A, tan A and sec A in terms of sin A. (c) Express sin A, sec A and tan A in terms of cot A.
hinglish_roman: (a) tan A = 1/√3 diya hai, identities se baaki ratios nikaalo. (b) cos A, tan A aur sec A ko sin A ke roop mein likho. (c) sin A, sec A aur tan A ko cot A ke roop mein likho.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Prove: (a) sec A(1 − sin A)(sec A + tan A) = 1 (b) (cosec θ − cot θ)² = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) (c) cos A/(1 + sin A) + (1 + sin A)/cos A = 2 sec A
hinglish_roman: Prove karo: (a) sec A(1 − sin A)(sec A + tan A) = 1 (b) (cosec θ − cot θ)² = (1 − cos θ)/(1 + cos θ) (c) cos A/(1 + sin A) + (1 + sin A)/cos A = 2 sec A

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Prove: (a) √[(1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A)] = sec A + tan A (b) (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A (c) (cosec A − sin A)(sec A − cos A) = 1/(tan A + cot A)
hinglish_roman: Prove karo: (a) √[(1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A)] = sec A + tan A (b) (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A (c) (cosec A − sin A)(sec A − cos A) = 1/(tan A + cot A)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Choose the correct option: (i) 9sec²A − 9tan²A = (A) 1 (B) 9 (C) 8 (D) 0. (ii) (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) = (A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) −1. (iii) (sec A + tan A)(1 − sin A) = (A) sec A (B) sin A (C) cosec A (D) cos A. (iv) (1 + tan²A)/(1 + cot²A) = (A) sec²A (B) −1 (C) cot²A (D) tan²A.
hinglish_roman: Sahi option chuno: (i) 9sec²A − 9tan²A = (A) 1 (B) 9 (C) 8 (D) 0. (ii) (1 + tan θ + sec θ)(1 + cot θ − cosec θ) = (A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) −1. (iii) (sec A + tan A)(1 − sin A) = (A) sec A (B) sin A (C) cosec A (D) cos A. (iv) (1 + tan²A)/(1 + cot²A) = (A) sec²A (B) −1 (C) cot²A (D) tan²A.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Fill in the blanks: The value of sin A or cos A never exceeds ______, whereas sec A or cosec A is always ______ 1.
hinglish_roman: Khaali jagah bharo: sin A ya cos A ki value kabhi ______ se zyada nahi hoti, jabki sec A ya cosec A hamesha 1 ke ______ hota hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Define line of sight, angle of elevation and angle of depression.
hinglish_roman: Line of sight, angle of elevation aur angle of depression define karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: To find the height of a minar without measuring it, what information is needed, and how is it used?
hinglish_roman: Minar ki oonchai bina naape nikaalne ke liye kya jaankari chahiye, aur use kaise lagaate hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) From a point 15 m from the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation of its top is 60°. Find the tower's height. (b) An observer 1.5 m tall is 28.5 m from a chimney and sees its top at 45°. Find the chimney's height.
hinglish_roman: (a) Tower ke paaye se 15 m door point se uski chot ka angle of elevation 60° hai. Tower ki oonchai nikaalo. (b) 1.5 m lamba observer chimney se 28.5 m door hai aur uski chot 45° pe dekhta hai. Chimney ki oonchai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: An electrician must reach a point 1.3 m below the top of a 5 m pole using a ladder inclined at 60° to the horizontal. Find the ladder's length and how far from the pole its foot should be. (√3 = 1.73)
hinglish_roman: Electrician ko 5 m ke khambe ki chot se 1.3 m neeche pahunchna hai, horizontal se 60° pe jhuki seedhi se. Seedhi ki lambai aur khambe se uske paaye ki doori nikaalo. (√3 = 1.73)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: From a point P the angle of elevation of the top of a 10 m building is 30°, and of the top of a flagstaff on it is 45°. Find the flagstaff's length and the building's distance from P. (√3 = 1.732)
hinglish_roman: Point P se 10 m building ki chot ka angle of elevation 30° hai, aur us par lage flagstaff ki chot ka 45°. Flagstaff ki lambai aur P se building ki doori nikaalo. (√3 = 1.732)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: The shadow of a tower is 40 m longer when the Sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. Find the tower's height.
hinglish_roman: Suraj ki altitude 30° hone pe tower ki parchhaai 60° hone ke mukaable 40 m lambi hoti hai. Tower ki oonchai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: From the top of a multi-storeyed building, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of an 8 m building are 30° and 45°. Find the height of the multi-storeyed building and the distance between them.
hinglish_roman: Ek oonchi building ki chot se 8 m building ki chot aur paaye ke angles of depression 30° aur 45° hain. Oonchi building ki oonchai aur dono ke beech ki doori nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: From a point on a bridge 3 m above the banks, the angles of depression of the banks on opposite sides of a river are 30° and 45°. Find the width of the river.
hinglish_roman: Kinaaron se 3 m oonche pul ke ek point se nadi ke dono taraf ke kinaaron ke angles of depression 30° aur 45° hain. Nadi ki chaudai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A circus artist climbs a 20 m rope tied from the top of a pole to the ground at 30°. Find the pole's height. (b) A kite flies at 60 m with its string at 60° to the ground. Find the string's length. (c) From 30 m away, a tower's top is seen at 30°. Find its height.
hinglish_roman: (a) Circus artist 20 m rassi chadh raha hai jo khambe ki chot se zameen tak 30° pe bandhi hai. Khambe ki oonchai nikaalo. (b) Patang 60 m oonchai pe hai aur dori zameen se 60° pe hai. Dori ki lambai nikaalo. (c) 30 m door se tower ki chot 30° pe dikhti hai. Oonchai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A tree breaks in a storm; its top touches the ground at 30°, 8 m from the foot. Find the tree's original height. (b) A slide for small children has its top at 1.5 m at 30°, and one for older children at 3 m at 60°. Find each slide's length.
hinglish_roman: (a) Toofaan mein ped toot jaata hai; uski chot zameen ko 30° pe, paaye se 8 m door chhooti hai. Ped ki asli oonchai nikaalo. (b) Chhote bachchon ki slide ki chot 1.5 m pe 30° pe hai, aur badon ki 3 m pe 60° pe. Har slide ki lambai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A 1.5 m tall boy stands near a 30 m building. As he walks towards it, the angle of elevation from his eyes to its top rises from 30° to 60°. How far did he walk?
hinglish_roman: 1.5 m lamba ladka 30 m building ke paas khada hai. Building ki taraf chalne pe uski aankh se chot ka angle of elevation 30° se 60° ho jaata hai. Woh kitna chala?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and top of a transmission tower on a 20 m building are 45° and 60°. Find the tower's height. (b) A 1.6 m statue stands on a pedestal; from a point on the ground the top of the statue is at 60° and the top of the pedestal at 45°. Find the pedestal's height.
hinglish_roman: (a) Zameen ke ek point se 20 m building pe lage transmission tower ke neeche aur upar ke angles of elevation 45° aur 60° hain. Tower ki oonchai nikaalo. (b) 1.6 m ki moorti ek chabootre pe hai; zameen ke ek point se moorti ki chot 60° pe aur chabootre ki chot 45° pe dikhti hai. Chabootre ki oonchai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A building's top is seen at 30° from the foot of a 50 m tower, and the tower's top at 60° from the foot of the building. Find the building's height. (b) Two equal poles stand on opposite sides of an 80 m road. From a point between them, their tops are at 60° and 30°. Find the height and the distances from the poles.
hinglish_roman: (a) 50 m tower ke paaye se building ki chot 30° pe, aur building ke paaye se tower ki chot 60° pe dikhti hai. Building ki oonchai nikaalo. (b) 80 m sadak ke dono taraf do barabar khambe hain. Beech ke ek point se unki choten 60° aur 30° pe dikhti hain. Oonchai aur khambon se dooriyaan nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A TV tower on one bank of a canal is seen at 60° from the opposite bank and at 30° from a point 20 m further back. Find the tower's height and the canal's width. (b) From the top of a 7 m building, a cable tower's top is at 60° elevation and its foot at 45° depression. Find the tower's height.
hinglish_roman: (a) Nahar ke ek kinaare pe TV tower saamne waale kinaare se 60° pe aur 20 m peeche ke point se 30° pe dikhta hai. Tower ki oonchai aur nahar ki chaudai nikaalo. (b) 7 m building ki chot se cable tower ki chot 60° elevation pe aur paaya 45° depression pe hai. Tower ki oonchai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) From a 75 m lighthouse, two ships one behind the other are seen at depressions 30° and 45°. Find the distance between them. (b) A 1.2 m girl sees a balloon at 88.2 m height at 60°, and later at 30°. How far did it travel?
hinglish_roman: (a) 75 m lighthouse se ek ke peeche ek do jahaaz 30° aur 45° depression pe dikhte hain. Unke beech ki doori nikaalo. (b) 1.2 m ki ladki 88.2 m oonchai pe gubbara 60° pe, aur baad mein 30° pe dekhti hai. Gubbara kitna chala?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A man on a tower sees a car approaching at a 30° angle of depression; 6 seconds later it is at 60°. How long will the car take to reach the foot of the tower?
hinglish_roman: Tower pe khada aadmi ek aati car ko 30° angle of depression pe dekhta hai; 6 second baad woh 60° pe hai. Car ko tower ke paaye tak pahunchne mein kitna samay lagega?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Compare the angle of elevation and the angle of depression. Why are they equal for two observers looking at each other?
hinglish_roman: Angle of elevation aur angle of depression ki tulna karo. Ek doosre ko dekhte do observers ke liye ye barabar kyun hote hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A ladder makes 60° with the ground and its foot is 2 m from a wall. The ladder's length is: (a) 2 m (b) 4 m (c) 2√3 m (d) 4√3 m
hinglish_roman: Seedhi zameen se 60° banaati hai aur uska paaya deewar se 2 m door hai. Seedhi ki lambai hai: (a) 2 m (b) 4 m (c) 2√3 m (d) 4√3 m

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What are the three possible positions of a line with respect to a circle?
hinglish_roman: Circle ke saapeksh ek line ki teen sambhav sthitiyaan kya hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is a tangent to a circle? What is the point of contact, and where does the word 'tangent' come from?
hinglish_roman: Circle ka tangent kya hota hai? Point of contact kya hai, aur 'tangent' shabd kahaan se aaya?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Explain with activities that exactly one tangent exists at a point on a circle and at most two tangents can be parallel to a given secant.
hinglish_roman: Activities se samjhaao ki circle ke ek point pe theek ek tangent hota hai aur kisi secant ke parallel zyada se zyada do tangents ho sakte hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: State and prove Theorem 10.1 about the tangent and the radius.
hinglish_roman: Tangent aur radius ke baare mein Theorem 10.1 batao aur prove karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Give everyday examples of tangents to a circle.
hinglish_roman: Circle ke tangents ke rozmarra ke udaharan do.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Fill in the blanks: (i) A tangent to a circle intersects it in ______ point(s). (ii) A line intersecting a circle in two points is called a ______. (iii) A circle can have at most ______ parallel tangents. (iv) The common point of a tangent and the circle is called the ______. (v) A circle can have ______ tangents.
hinglish_roman: Khaali jagah bharo: (i) Circle ka tangent use ______ point(s) pe kaatta hai. (ii) Circle ko do points pe kaatne waali line ______ kehlaati hai. (iii) Circle ke zyada se zyada ______ parallel tangents ho sakte hain. (iv) Tangent aur circle ke common point ko ______ kehte hain. (v) Circle ke ______ tangents ho sakte hain.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point inside, on and outside the circle?
hinglish_roman: Circle ke andar, circle pe aur circle ke bahar ke point se circle pe kitne tangents kheenche ja sakte hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. What else follows?
hinglish_roman: Prove karo ki bahar ke point se circle pe kheenche gaye tangents ki lambaiyaan barabar hoti hain. Isse aur kya nikalta hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Prove that in two concentric circles, a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle is bisected at the point of contact. (b) Two concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. Find the length of such a chord.
hinglish_roman: (a) Prove karo ki do concentric circles mein bade circle ki chord jo chhote circle ko chhooti hai, point of contact pe bisect hoti hai. (b) Do concentric circles ki radii 5 cm aur 3 cm hain. Aisi chord ki lambai nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Two tangents TP and TQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point T. Prove that ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.
hinglish_roman: Centre O waale circle pe bahar ke point T se do tangents TP aur TQ kheenche gaye. Prove karo ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: PQ is a chord of length 8 cm of a circle of radius 5 cm. The tangents at P and Q meet at T. Find TP.
hinglish_roman: PQ, 5 cm radius waale circle ki 8 cm lambi chord hai. P aur Q pe tangents T pe milte hain. TP nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Choose the correct option: (i) A tangent PQ at P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the centre at Q with OQ = 12 cm. PQ = (A) 12 cm (B) 13 cm (C) 8.5 cm (D) √119 cm. (ii) The tangent from Q is 24 cm and Q is 25 cm from the centre. The radius is (A) 7 cm (B) 12 cm (C) 15 cm (D) 24.5 cm.
hinglish_roman: Sahi option chuno: (i) 5 cm radius waale circle ke P pe tangent PQ, centre se guzarti line ko Q pe milta hai jahan OQ = 12 cm. PQ = (A) 12 cm (B) 13 cm (C) 8.5 cm (D) √119 cm. (ii) Q se tangent 24 cm hai aur Q centre se 25 cm door hai. Radius hai (A) 7 cm (B) 12 cm (C) 15 cm (D) 24.5 cm.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Choose the correct option: (i) TP and TQ are tangents to a circle with centre O and ∠POQ = 110°. ∠PTQ = (A) 60° (B) 70° (C) 80° (D) 90°. (ii) Tangents PA and PB from P are inclined at 80°. ∠POA = (A) 50° (B) 60° (C) 70° (D) 80°.
hinglish_roman: Sahi option chuno: (i) TP aur TQ, centre O waale circle ke tangents hain aur ∠POQ = 110°. ∠PTQ = (A) 60° (B) 70° (C) 80° (D) 90°. (ii) P se tangents PA aur PB, 80° pe jhuke hain. ∠POA = (A) 50° (B) 60° (C) 70° (D) 80°.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Prove: (a) tangents at the ends of a diameter are parallel; (b) the perpendicular to a tangent at its point of contact passes through the centre; (c) the angle between two tangents from an external point is supplementary to the angle subtended at the centre by the segment joining the points of contact.
hinglish_roman: Prove karo: (a) diameter ke siron pe tangents parallel hote hain; (b) tangent ke point of contact pe perpendicular centre se guzarta hai; (c) bahar ke point se do tangents ke beech ka angle, points of contact ko jodne waale segment se centre pe bane angle ka supplementary hota hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle. Prove AB + CD = AD + BC. (b) Hence prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
hinglish_roman: (a) Quadrilateral ABCD ek circle ko gherta hai. Prove karo AB + CD = AD + BC. (b) Isse prove karo ki circle ko gherne waala parallelogram rhombus hota hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) The tangent from A, 5 cm from the centre, is 4 cm. Find the radius. (b) △ABC circumscribes a circle of radius 4 cm, and the point of contact D divides BC into BD = 8 cm and DC = 6 cm. Find AB and AC.
hinglish_roman: (a) Centre se 5 cm door A se tangent 4 cm hai. Radius nikaalo. (b) △ABC, 4 cm radius waale circle ko gherta hai, aur contact point D, BC ko BD = 8 cm aur DC = 6 cm mein baantta hai. AB aur AC nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: XY and X′Y′ are parallel tangents to a circle with centre O, and tangent AB at C meets XY at A and X′Y′ at B. Prove ∠AOB = 90°.
hinglish_roman: XY aur X′Y′, centre O waale circle ke parallel tangents hain, aur C pe tangent AB, XY ko A pe aur X′Y′ ko B pe milta hai. Prove karo ∠AOB = 90°.

subject: Mathematics
original_english:
Assertion (A): No tangent can be drawn to a circle from a point inside it.
Reason (R): Every line through an interior point of a circle cuts the circle at two points.
hinglish_roman:
Assertion (A): Circle ke andar ke point se circle pe koi tangent nahi kheencha ja sakta.
Reason (R): Circle ke andar ke point se guzarti har line circle ko do points pe kaatti hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What are a sector and a segment of a circle? What are minor and major sectors and segments?
hinglish_roman: Circle ka sector aur segment kya hota hai? Minor aur major sectors aur segments kya hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Derive the formulas for the area of a sector and the length of an arc of angle θ, and give the area of a segment.
hinglish_roman: θ angle ke sector ka area aur arc ki lambai ke formulas nikaalo, aur segment ka area batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the area of a sector of radius 4 cm and angle 30°, and of the corresponding major sector. (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: 4 cm radius aur 30° angle waale sector ka area, aur sambandhit major sector ka area nikaalo. (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the area of the segment of a circle of radius 21 cm with ∠AOB = 120°. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: 21 cm radius waale circle mein ∠AOB = 120° waale segment ka area nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find the area of a sector of radius 6 cm and angle 60°. (b) Find the area of a quadrant of a circle of circumference 22 cm. (c) A 14 cm minute hand sweeps for 5 minutes. Find the area swept. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) 6 cm radius aur 60° angle waale sector ka area nikaalo. (b) 22 cm paridhi waale circle ke quadrant ka area nikaalo. (c) 14 cm ki minute ki sui 5 minute mein kitna area ghoomti hai? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the area of (i) the minor segment (ii) the major sector. (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: 10 cm radius waale circle ki ek chord centre pe right angle banaati hai. Area nikaalo: (i) minor segment (ii) major sector. (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: In a circle of radius 21 cm, an arc subtends 60° at the centre. Find (i) the arc length (ii) the sector area (iii) the segment area. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: 21 cm radius waale circle mein ek arc centre pe 60° banaata hai. Nikaalo (i) arc ki lambai (ii) sector ka area (iii) segment ka area. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends 60° at the centre. Find the minor and major segment areas. (b) A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends 120°. Find the segment area. (π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73)
hinglish_roman: (a) 15 cm radius waale circle ki chord centre pe 60° banaati hai. Minor aur major segment ke area nikaalo. (b) 12 cm radius waale circle ki chord 120° banaati hai. Segment ka area nikaalo. (π = 3.14, √3 = 1.73)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a 15 m square field with a 5 m rope. Find (i) the area it can graze (ii) the increase in grazing area if the rope were 10 m. (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: 15 m ke square khet ke ek kone pe khoonte se ghoda 5 m rassi se bandha hai. Nikaalo (i) woh kitne area mein char sakta hai (ii) rassi 10 m ho toh charne ka area kitna badhega. (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A brooch is a silver-wire circle of diameter 35 mm with 5 diameters dividing it into 10 equal sectors. Find the total wire length and the area of each sector. (b) An umbrella with 8 equally spaced ribs is a flat circle of radius 45 cm. Find the area between two consecutive ribs. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Ek brooch 35 mm diameter ka chaandi ke taar ka circle hai jisme 5 diameters use 10 barabar sectors mein baantte hain. Kul taar ki lambai aur har sector ka area nikaalo. (b) 8 barabar doori ki teeliyon waala chhaata 45 cm radius ka chapta circle hai. Do lagaataar teeliyon ke beech ka area nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A car has two non-overlapping wipers, each 25 cm long, sweeping 115°. Find the total area cleaned per sweep. (b) A lighthouse spreads red light over an 80° sector up to 16.5 km. Find the sea area warned. (π = 22/7 for (a), 3.14 for (b))
hinglish_roman: (a) Car mein do wipers hain jo overlap nahi karte, har ek 25 cm lamba, 115° ghoomta hai. Har sweep mein kul saaf area nikaalo. (b) Lighthouse 80° ke sector mein 16.5 km tak laal roshni phailaata hai. Chetaavni waala samudri area nikaalo. ((a) ke liye π = 22/7, (b) ke liye 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A round table cover of radius 28 cm has six equal designs, each a segment cut off by a 60° chord. Find the cost of making them at ₹0.35 per cm². (π = 22/7, √3 = 1.7)
hinglish_roman: 28 cm radius ke gol table cover pe chhe barabar designs hain, har ek 60° chord se kata segment. ₹0.35 prati cm² ki dar se banaane ki laagat nikaalo. (π = 22/7, √3 = 1.7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: The area of a sector of angle p (in degrees) of a circle of radius R is: (A) (p/180) × 2πR (B) (p/180) × πR² (C) (p/360) × 2πR (D) (p/720) × 2πR²
hinglish_roman: R radius waale circle ke p (degrees) angle ke sector ka area hai: (A) (p/180) × 2πR (B) (p/180) × πR² (C) (p/360) × 2πR (D) (p/720) × 2πR²

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Differentiate between a sector and a segment of a circle. How are their areas related?
hinglish_roman: Circle ke sector aur segment mein antar batao. Unke area kaise jude hain?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How do we find the surface area of a solid made by combining basic solids? Why is it not the sum of the total surface areas of the parts?
hinglish_roman: Basic solids ko jodkar bane solid ka surface area kaise nikaalte hain? Ye hisson ke total surface areas ka jod kyun nahi hota?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How does finding the volume of a combined solid differ from finding its surface area?
hinglish_roman: Jode hue solid ka volume nikaalna uska surface area nikaalne se kaise alag hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Rasheed's top is a cone surmounted by a hemisphere, 5 cm tall overall with diameter 3.5 cm. Find the area he has to colour. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: Rasheed ka lattu ek hemisphere pe cone hai, kul 5 cm ooncha aur 3.5 cm diameter. Use kitna area rang karna hai? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A decorative block is a 5 cm cube with a hemisphere of diameter 4.2 cm on top. Find its total surface area. (b) A cubical block of side 7 cm is surmounted by a hemisphere. What is the greatest possible diameter of the hemisphere, and what is the surface area? (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Ek decorative block 5 cm ka cube hai jiske upar 4.2 cm diameter ka hemisphere hai. Iska total surface area nikaalo. (b) 7 cm side ke cube pe hemisphere laga hai. Hemisphere ka sabse bada sambhav diameter kya hai, aur surface area kitna hai? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A toy rocket is a cone on a cylinder: total height 26 cm, cone height 6 cm, cone base diameter 5 cm, cylinder diameter 3 cm. The cone is painted orange and the cylinder yellow. Find each area. (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: Khilona rocket cylinder pe cone hai: kul oonchai 26 cm, cone ki oonchai 6 cm, cone ke base ka diameter 5 cm, cylinder ka diameter 3 cm. Cone orange aur cylinder yellow rangna hai. Dono area nikaalo. (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Mayank's bird-bath is a cylinder 1.45 m high, radius 30 cm, with a hemispherical depression at one end. Find its total surface area. (b) Two 64 cm³ cubes are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the cuboid. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Mayank ka bird-bath 1.45 m ooncha, 30 cm radius ka cylinder hai jiske ek sire pe hemispherical gaddha hai. Iska total surface area nikaalo. (b) 64 cm³ ke do cubes sire se sira jode gaye. Cuboid ka surface area nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A vessel is a hollow hemisphere (diameter 14 cm) with a hollow cylinder on it; total height 13 cm. Find its inner surface area. (b) A toy is a cone of radius 3.5 cm on a hemisphere of the same radius, total height 15.5 cm. Find its total surface area. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Bartan khokhle hemisphere (diameter 14 cm) pe khokhla cylinder hai; kul oonchai 13 cm. Andar ka surface area nikaalo. (b) Khilona 3.5 cm radius ka cone hai jo same radius ke hemisphere pe hai, kul oonchai 15.5 cm. Total surface area nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A hemispherical depression is cut from one face of a cube of edge l, with diameter l. Find the surface area of the remaining solid. (b) A capsule is a cylinder with hemispherical ends: total length 14 mm, diameter 5 mm. Find its surface area. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Edge l waale cube ke ek face se l diameter ka hemispherical gaddha kaata gaya. Bache solid ka surface area nikaalo. (b) Capsule cylinder hai jiske dono sire hemisphere hain: kul lambai 14 mm, diameter 5 mm. Surface area nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A tent is a cylinder (height 2.1 m, diameter 4 m) with a conical top of slant height 2.8 m. Find the canvas area (no base) and its cost at ₹500 per m². (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: Tambu cylinder (oonchai 2.1 m, diameter 4 m) hai jiske upar 2.8 m slant height ka conical top hai. Canvas ka area (base nahi) aur ₹500 prati m² se laagat nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A conical cavity of the same height (2.4 cm) and diameter (1.4 cm) is hollowed from a solid cylinder. Find the TSA of the remaining solid to the nearest cm². (b) A hemisphere is scooped out from each end of a solid cylinder of height 10 cm and radius 3.5 cm. Find the TSA. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Solid cylinder (oonchai 2.4 cm, diameter 1.4 cm) se same oonchai aur diameter ki conical cavity nikaali gayi. Bache solid ka TSA nazdeeki cm² tak nikaalo. (b) 10 cm oonche, 3.5 cm radius ke solid cylinder ke dono siron se hemisphere nikaale gaye. TSA nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Shanta's shed is a cuboid (base 7 m × 15 m, height 8 m) surmounted by a half cylinder. Find the volume of air it holds. Machinery takes 300 m³ and 20 workers take 0.08 m³ each. How much air remains? (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: Shanta ka shed cuboid (base 7 m × 15 m, oonchai 8 m) hai jiske upar aadha cylinder hai. Usme kitni hawa samaati hai? Machinery 300 m³ aur 20 mazdoor 0.08 m³ har ek lete hain. Kitni hawa bachti hai? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A juice seller's glass has inner diameter 5 cm and height 10 cm, but a raised hemispherical bottom. Find the apparent and actual capacity. (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: Juice waale ke glass ka andar ka diameter 5 cm aur oonchai 10 cm hai, par tala hemisphere jaisa upar utha hai. Dikhne waali aur asli capacity nikaalo. (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A toy is a cone (height 2 cm, base diameter 4 cm) on a hemisphere. Find its volume and the difference from the circumscribing cylinder's volume. (π = 3.14) (b) A cone stands on a hemisphere, both of radius 1 cm, with cone height = radius. Find the volume in terms of π.
hinglish_roman: (a) Khilona hemisphere pe cone (oonchai 2 cm, base diameter 4 cm) hai. Iska volume aur gherne waale cylinder ke volume se fark nikaalo. (π = 3.14) (b) 1 cm radius ke hemisphere pe same radius ka cone hai, cone ki oonchai = radius. Volume π mein nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Rachel's model is a cylinder with a cone at each end: diameter 3 cm, total length 12 cm, each cone 2 cm high. Find the volume of air inside. (b) A pen stand is a 15 × 10 × 3.5 cm cuboid with four conical depressions of radius 0.5 cm and depth 1.4 cm. Find the volume of wood. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Rachel ka model cylinder hai jiske dono siron pe cone hain: diameter 3 cm, kul lambai 12 cm, har cone 2 cm ooncha. Andar ki hawa ka volume nikaalo. (b) Pen stand 15 × 10 × 3.5 cm ka cuboid hai jisme 0.5 cm radius aur 1.4 cm gehraai ke chaar conical gaddhe hain. Lakdi ka volume nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A gulab jamun is a cylinder with hemispherical ends, length 5 cm and diameter 2.8 cm, and contains syrup up to 30% of its volume. How much syrup is in 45 gulab jamuns? (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: Gulab jamun cylinder hai jiske dono sire hemisphere hain, lambai 5 cm aur diameter 2.8 cm, aur usme volume ka 30% chaashni hai. 45 gulab jamuns mein kitni chaashni hai? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A vessel is an inverted cone 8 cm high with an open top of radius 5 cm, full of water. Lead shots (spheres of radius 0.5 cm) are dropped in until one-fourth of the water flows out. How many shots were dropped? (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: Bartan ulta cone hai, 8 cm ooncha, khula upar 5 cm radius ka, paani se bhara. 0.5 cm radius ke lead ke goliyaan daali gayi jab tak chauthaai paani bahar na nikal gaya. Kitni goliyaan daali? (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) An iron pole is a cylinder (height 220 cm, diameter 24 cm) topped by another (height 60 cm, radius 8 cm). Find its mass if 1 cm³ of iron weighs 8 g. (π = 3.14) (b) A cone (height 120 cm, radius 60 cm) on a hemisphere (radius 60 cm) is placed upright in a cylinder of radius 60 cm and height 180 cm full of water. Find the water left. (π = 22/7)
hinglish_roman: (a) Lohe ka khamba cylinder (oonchai 220 cm, diameter 24 cm) hai jiske upar doosra (oonchai 60 cm, radius 8 cm) hai. 1 cm³ loha 8 g ka ho toh mass nikaalo. (π = 3.14) (b) Hemisphere (radius 60 cm) pe cone (oonchai 120 cm, radius 60 cm) ko paani se bhare cylinder (radius 60 cm, oonchai 180 cm) mein seedha rakha. Bacha paani nikaalo. (π = 22/7)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: A spherical glass vessel (inner diameter 8.5 cm) has a cylindrical neck 8 cm long and 2 cm in diameter. A child measures its volume as 345 cm³. Is she correct? (π = 3.14)
hinglish_roman: Gol kaanch ke bartan (andar ka diameter 8.5 cm) ki 8 cm lambi aur 2 cm diameter ki cylindrical gardan hai. Ek bachchi ne iska volume 345 cm³ naapa. Kya woh sahi hai? (π = 3.14)

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Give everyday examples of objects that are combinations of basic solids, naming the solids.
hinglish_roman: Rozmarra ki un cheezon ke udaharan do jo basic solids ko jodkar bani hain, solids ke naam ke saath.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How is the mean of grouped data found? What is a class mark, and why does the grouped mean differ slightly from the exact mean?
hinglish_roman: Grouped data ka mean kaise nikaalte hain? Class mark kya hai, aur grouped mean asli mean se thoda alag kyun aata hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Compare the direct, assumed mean and step-deviation methods for finding the mean of grouped data. When is each convenient?
hinglish_roman: Grouped data ka mean nikaalne ke direct, assumed mean aur step-deviation methods ki tulna karo. Har ek kab suvidhajanak hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Find the mean percentage of female teachers in rural primary schools: classes 15–25, 25–35, …, 75–85 with frequencies 6, 11, 7, 4, 4, 2, 1. Use all three methods.
hinglish_roman: Rural primary schools mein mahila teachers ka mean percentage nikaalo: classes 15–25, 25–35, …, 75–85 aur frequencies 6, 11, 7, 4, 4, 2, 1. Teenon methods lagao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Wickets taken by 45 bowlers: 20–60 (7), 60–100 (5), 100–150 (16), 150–250 (12), 250–350 (2), 350–450 (3). Find the mean and say what it signifies.
hinglish_roman: 45 bowlers ke wickets: 20–60 (7), 60–100 (5), 100–150 (16), 150–250 (12), 250–350 (2), 350–450 (3). Mean nikaalo aur batao ye kya darshaata hai.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is the modal class? State the formula for the mode of grouped data.
hinglish_roman: Modal class kya hai? Grouped data ke mode ka formula batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Wickets in 10 matches: 2, 6, 4, 5, 0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3. Find the mode. (b) Family sizes of 20 households: 1–3 (7), 3–5 (8), 5–7 (2), 7–9 (2), 9–11 (1). Find the mode.
hinglish_roman: (a) 10 matches mein wickets: 2, 6, 4, 5, 0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 3. Mode nikaalo. (b) 20 gharon ka parivaar size: 1–3 (7), 3–5 (8), 5–7 (2), 7–9 (2), 9–11 (1). Mode nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: For the marks of 30 students (10–25: 2, 25–40: 3, 40–55: 7, 55–70: 6, 70–85: 6, 85–100: 6), find the mode and compare it with the mean of 62.
hinglish_roman: 30 students ke marks (10–25: 2, 25–40: 3, 40–55: 7, 55–70: 6, 70–85: 6, 85–100: 6) ka mode nikaalo aur 62 ke mean se tulna karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Hospital patients by age: 5–15 (6), 15–25 (11), 25–35 (21), 35–45 (23), 45–55 (14), 55–65 (5). Find the mode and mean and interpret them.
hinglish_roman: Hospital ke mareez umar ke hisaab se: 5–15 (6), 15–25 (11), 25–35 (21), 35–45 (23), 45–55 (14), 55–65 (5). Mode aur mean nikaalo aur unka matlab batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What is cumulative frequency? Distinguish between 'less than' and 'more than' cumulative frequency distributions.
hinglish_roman: Cumulative frequency kya hai? 'Less than' aur 'more than' cumulative frequency distributions mein antar batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: How is the median of ungrouped and grouped data found? State the median formula.
hinglish_roman: Ungrouped aur grouped data ka median kaise nikaalte hain? Median ka formula batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Marks of 53 students give cumulative frequencies 5, 8, 12, 15, 18, 22, 29, 38, 45, 53 for 0–10, …, 90–100. Find the median. (b) Heights of 51 girls: less than 140: 4, 145: 11, 150: 29, 155: 40, 160: 46, 165: 51. Find the median height.
hinglish_roman: (a) 53 students ke marks ki cumulative frequencies 0–10, …, 90–100 ke liye 5, 8, 12, 15, 18, 22, 29, 38, 45, 53 hain. Median nikaalo. (b) 51 ladkiyon ki height: 140 se kam: 4, 145: 11, 150: 29, 155: 40, 160: 46, 165: 51. Median height nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Electricity consumption of 68 consumers: 65–85 (4), 85–105 (5), 105–125 (13), 125–145 (20), 145–165 (14), 165–185 (8), 185–205 (4). Find the median, mean and mode and compare them.
hinglish_roman: 68 upbhoktaon ki bijli khapat: 65–85 (4), 85–105 (5), 105–125 (13), 125–145 (20), 145–165 (14), 165–185 (8), 185–205 (4). Median, mean aur mode nikaalo aur tulna karo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Policy holders' ages (cumulative): below 20: 2, 25: 6, 30: 24, 35: 45, 40: 78, 45: 89, 50: 92, 55: 98, 60: 100. Find the median age. (b) Weights of 30 students: 40–45 (2), 45–50 (3), 50–55 (8), 55–60 (6), 60–65 (6), 65–70 (3), 70–75 (2). Find the median weight.
hinglish_roman: (a) Policy holders ki umar (cumulative): 20 se neeche: 2, 25: 6, 30: 24, 35: 45, 40: 78, 45: 89, 50: 92, 55: 98, 60: 100. Median umar nikaalo. (b) 30 students ka vajan: 40–45 (2), 45–50 (3), 50–55 (8), 55–60 (6), 60–65 (6), 65–70 (3), 70–75 (2). Median vajan nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: When should the mean, median or mode be used? State the empirical relationship between them.
hinglish_roman: Mean, median ya mode kab use karna chahiye? Inke beech ka empirical sambandh batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: For the number of letters in 100 surnames: 1–4 (6), 4–7 (30), 7–10 (40), 10–13 (16), 13–16 (4), 16–19 (4), find the median, mean and mode.
hinglish_roman: 100 surnames mein aksharon ki sankhya: 1–4 (6), 4–7 (30), 7–10 (40), 10–13 (16), 13–16 (4), 16–19 (4) ke liye median, mean aur mode nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Fill in the blanks: (i) The class with the maximum frequency is the ______ class. (ii) The class whose cumulative frequency is just greater than n/2 is the ______ class. (iii) 3 Median = ______ + 2 Mean.
hinglish_roman: Khaali jagah bharo: (i) Sabse zyada frequency waali class ______ class hai. (ii) Jis class ki cumulative frequency n/2 se theek zyada ho woh ______ class hai. (iii) 3 Median = ______ + 2 Mean.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Define the theoretical (classical) probability of an event. Who gave this definition?
hinglish_roman: Kisi event ki theoretical (classical) probability define karo. Ye definition kisne di?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Compare experimental (empirical) and theoretical probability. Why is theoretical probability needed?
hinglish_roman: Experimental (empirical) aur theoretical probability ki tulna karo. Theoretical probability ki zaroorat kyun hai?

subject: Mathematics
original_english: What are equally likely outcomes? Give examples and a non-example.
hinglish_roman: Equally likely outcomes kya hote hain? Udaharan aur ek ulta udaharan do.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Explain elementary events, complementary events, sure events and impossible events, with the range of probability.
hinglish_roman: Elementary events, complementary events, sure events aur impossible events samjhaao, probability ki range ke saath.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Briefly describe the history of probability theory.
hinglish_roman: Probability theory ka itihaas sankshep mein batao.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Find P(head) and P(tail) for one coin toss. (b) Kritika draws one ball from a bag with one red, one blue and one yellow ball. Find each probability. (c) A die is thrown once: find P(number > 4) and P(number ≤ 4).
hinglish_roman: (a) Ek baar sikka uchhaalne pe P(head) aur P(tail) nikaalo. (b) Kritika ek laal, ek neeli aur ek peeli gend waale thaile se ek gend nikaalti hai. Har probability nikaalo. (c) Die ek baar phenkne pe P(number > 4) aur P(number ≤ 4) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) One card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52. Find P(ace) and P(not an ace). (b) Sangeeta's probability of winning a tennis match against Reshma is 0.62. Find Reshma's probability of winning.
hinglish_roman: (a) 52 ke achchhe se phente deck se ek card nikaala. P(ikka) aur P(ikka nahi) nikaalo. (b) Sangeeta ke Reshma se tennis match jeetne ki probability 0.62 hai. Reshma ke jeetne ki probability nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Savita and Hamida are friends. Ignoring leap years, find P(different birthdays) and P(same birthday). (b) In a group of 3 students, P(2 students do not share a birthday) = 0.992. Find P(they share a birthday).
hinglish_roman: (a) Savita aur Hamida dost hain. Leap year chhodkar P(alag birthdays) aur P(same birthday) nikaalo. (b) 3 students ke group mein P(2 students ka birthday same nahi) = 0.992. P(unka birthday same) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A class of 40 has 25 girls and 15 boys; one name is drawn. Find P(girl) and P(boy). (b) A box has 3 blue, 2 white and 4 red marbles. Find P(white), P(blue), P(red). (c) A bag has 3 red and 5 black balls. Find P(red) and P(not red).
hinglish_roman: (a) 40 ki class mein 25 ladkiyaan aur 15 ladke hain; ek naam nikaala. P(ladki) aur P(ladka) nikaalo. (b) Box mein 3 neeli, 2 safed aur 4 laal goliyaan hain. P(safed), P(neeli), P(laal) nikaalo. (c) Thaile mein 3 laal aur 5 kaali gendein hain. P(laal) aur P(laal nahi) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) Harpreet tosses two different coins together. Find P(at least one head). (b) Hanif tosses a coin 3 times and wins only if all results are the same. Find P(Hanif loses).
hinglish_roman: (a) Harpreet do alag sikke ek saath uchhaalti hai. P(kam se kam ek head) nikaalo. (b) Hanif sikka 3 baar uchhaalta hai aur tabhi jeetta hai jab teenon nateeje same hon. P(Hanif haare) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: Two dice (blue and grey) are thrown. How many outcomes are there? Find P(sum = 8), P(sum = 13), P(sum ≤ 12), and the full table of P(sum) for sums 2 to 12.
hinglish_roman: Do dice (neela aur grey) phenke gaye. Kitne outcomes hain? P(jod = 8), P(jod = 13), P(jod ≤ 12), aur jod 2 se 12 tak ki poori P(jod) table nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52. Find P of: (i) a red king (ii) a face card (iii) a red face card (iv) the jack of hearts (v) a spade (vi) the queen of diamonds.
hinglish_roman: 52 ke achchhe se phente deck se ek card nikaala. P nikaalo: (i) laal badshah (ii) face card (iii) laal face card (iv) paan ka gulaam (v) hukum (vi) eent ki begum.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) The ten, jack, queen, king and ace of diamonds are shuffled face down and one is picked. Find P(queen). If the queen is put aside, find P(ace) and P(queen) for the second card. (b) A lot of 20 bulbs has 4 defective. Find P(defective). If a good bulb is drawn and not replaced, find P(next is not defective).
hinglish_roman: (a) Eent ke dahla, gulaam, begum, badshah aur ikka ulte phente gaye aur ek uthaaya. P(begum) nikaalo. Agar begum alag rakh di, toh doosre card ke liye P(ikka) aur P(begum) nikaalo. (b) 20 bulbs mein 4 kharaab hain. P(kharaab) nikaalo. Agar ek achchha bulb nikaalkar wapas na rakhein, toh P(agla kharaab nahi) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A box has 90 discs numbered 1 to 90. Find P of a two-digit number, a perfect square, and a number divisible by 5. (b) A die thrown once: find P(prime), P(number between 2 and 6), P(odd). (c) A spinner shows 1–8 equally likely: find P(8), P(odd), P(> 2), P(< 9).
hinglish_roman: (a) Box mein 1 se 90 tak numbered 90 discs hain. Do-ank number, perfect square aur 5 se divisible number ki P nikaalo. (b) Die ek baar: P(prime), P(2 aur 6 ke beech), P(odd) nikaalo. (c) Spinner 1–8 barabar sambhav: P(8), P(odd), P(> 2), P(< 9) nikaalo.

subject: Mathematics
original_english: (a) A piggy bank has hundred 50p coins, fifty ₹1, twenty ₹2 and ten ₹5 coins. Find P(50p) and P(not ₹5). (b) A box has 5 red, 8 white and 4 green marbles. Find P(red), P(white), P(not green). (c) A die's faces show A, B, C, D, E, A. Find P(A) and P(D).
